summary: Builds the people, partnerships, funding and operating infrastructure King’s needs to create high-quality experiential opportunities, connect students and graduates with employers in the UK and internationally, widen access to purposeful global experience, remove barriers to participation, and support successful transition into graduate futures.
detailSummary:
King’s already holds extensive relationships with employers, industry, public bodies, community and third-sector organisations, civic and cultural partners, international organisations and alumni. It also has strong careers expertise, an established Global Mobility service, pockets of student-opportunity funding, philanthropic relationships and locally developed processes for experiential activity. These assets are distributed across faculties and professional services and are not yet consistently visible, coordinated or activated as one coherent institutional engine for opportunity and graduate success.

The proposition therefore brings together six connected capabilities. First, King’s will preserve and strengthen the common operating infrastructure through which experiential opportunities are sourced, designed, approved, promoted, delivered, supported and evaluated. This includes clearer roles across central teams and faculties; proportionate standards for quality, accessibility, safeguarding, risk, data and student support; common templates and agreements; simpler contracting and payment routes; better partner intelligence; and a clearer institutional opportunity pipeline. Delivery remains distributed: the infrastructure should make local delivery easier, safer and more consistent rather than centralising it.

Second, King’s will retain a dedicated domestic experiential opportunity translation and partnership-infrastructure envelope. From 2027/28, a £300,000 p.a. Core planning assumption will support the faculty-facing and shared operational capacity needed to turn UK employer, alumni, civic, cultural, community and other external relationships into well-formed student opportunities. This is the practical translation layer between a relationship or external proposition and a student-ready experience: brokerage, scoping, learning-design translation, contracting, partner onboarding, payments, administration and handover into near-curriculum and flexible opportunity routes. The exact role mix should be informed by the first-year capability review and demand emerging through 2.1.4, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4.

Third, King’s will create dedicated international employer-engagement capacity. The immediate phase will protect and deepen the existing East Asia portfolio through a G6 Employer Relations & Insights Manager and a G5 East Asia Adviser. From September 2027, two further G5 Advisers will extend capacity across South and South East Asia and Europe and North America. A £50,000 annual non-pay envelope will support employer-facing and in-country activity. This capability is intended to improve access to relevant employers and labour-market intelligence for students and graduates while also strengthening King’s employability proposition in strategically important recruitment markets.

Fourth, King’s will strengthen Global Mobility with two incremental opportunity-development posts from September 2027: one G6 and one G5. These roles are intended to add growth and translation capacity rather than duplicate the existing service’s core exchange administration. Working with the established Global Mobility team, faculties and King’s Edge, they will grow and broker a broader mix of purposeful outward mobility, including shorter-form, experiential, work-related and other accessible international opportunities; connect mobility more deliberately to skills and graduate futures; and help turn overseas partnerships and propositions into student-ready opportunities that can feed the flexible and near-curriculum offer.

Fifth, King’s will establish a small Graduate Transitions function from May 2027, initially comprising a G7 Head of Graduate Transitions and a G6 Graduate Transitions Coach. The function will move support beyond a predominantly reactive model by using Careers Readiness and other available data to identify graduates who may be at risk of poorer outcomes and provide targeted coaching, job-search support, employer referral and other interventions through the critical post-completion period captured by Graduate Outcomes.

Sixth, the deliverable will retain the existing access and opportunity-growth work. King’s will review and consolidate financial support for students undertaking employment-enhancing and developmental activity, with the intended direction of a coherent Student Opportunities Fund combining low-friction microbursaries of around £150-£250 with more substantial awards of around £4,000 for genuine out-of-pocket participation costs. Any new award pot sits outside the King’s Edge mobilisation ask and requires a separate institutional, consolidated-fund, philanthropic or other funding route. Alumni engagement and philanthropy will also be used deliberately to grow the supply of opportunity, including service-learning and social-good projects and models in which paid PhD project leads can mobilise flexible opportunities for wider student participation.

The causal logic is that King’s can create more meaningful and accessible experience, connect it more effectively to employers and graduate destinations, widen access to purposeful international experience, and improve institutional efficiency by joining up assets it already holds with targeted new capabilities. The current Core resource proposition has a £300,000 p.a. domestic experiential opportunity translation and partnership-infrastructure envelope from 2027/28, plus £449,969 annualised specified staffing for international employer engagement, Graduate Transitions and Global Mobility opportunity development, plus a £50,000 international employer-engagement non-pay envelope. The fully mobilised annualised Core ask for 2.2.2 is therefore £799,969, excluding any separately funded Student Opportunities Fund award pot. All grade-based staffing figures are treated as fully loaded planning costs including employer National Insurance and pension/superannuation and should be validated with Finance/HR before approval; the £300,000 domestic envelope is likewise an all-in staffing and operating envelope whose eventual workforce mix must be costed on the same basis.

caseForChange.problem: King’s has substantial external relationships, careers expertise, an established Global Mobility service, alumni connection and pockets of student-opportunity funding, but the infrastructure that turns these assets into opportunity and positive graduate destinations is fragmented. Relationship management, opportunity design, contracting, risk, payments, partner intelligence, international employer engagement, global opportunity development, graduate support and financial-access mechanisms can operate separately. Domestic external relationships are not always translated into student-ready experiential opportunities at the scale required, and the institution has limited incremental capacity to grow and translate a broader portfolio of purposeful outward mobility beyond existing core provision. This creates duplicated effort, missed connections, uneven access, fragile international employer capability and a reactive transition model for graduates who need additional support.
caseForChange.opportunity: King’s can create a stronger institutional engine that connects domestic experiential opportunity translation, shared operating infrastructure, employer relationships, international labour-market capability, global mobility opportunity development, proactive graduate transition, alumni engagement, philanthropy and student financial support. Shared standards can reduce friction and duplication without centralising delivery. Dedicated domestic translation capacity can turn external interest into well-formed projects, placements, live briefs, challenges and other experiential routes. Dedicated international employer capacity can protect and expand strategically valuable relationships. Incremental Global Mobility capacity can grow shorter-form and employability-linked international opportunities without displacing the existing team’s core exchange work. A small Graduate Transitions function can target support where it is most needed. A coherent Student Opportunities Fund and philanthropic propositions can remove financial barriers and grow opportunity supply.
caseForChange.whyNow: King’s Edge is increasing the volume and ambition of experiential opportunity within and beyond the curriculum at the same time as the graduate labour market becomes more challenging and employability becomes more important to student choice. Growth through 2.1.4, 2.2.3 and 2.2.4 will create additional demand for domestic partner sourcing, brokerage and opportunity translation, including global opportunity as a thematic priority. Existing East Asia employability activity has demonstrated value but is unsupported by dedicated resource and has displaced domestic employer-engagement capacity. The existing Global Mobility team already facilitates study abroad and overseas traineeships, but Edge creates a case for additional opportunity-development capacity focused on growth, accessibility and stronger connection to graduate futures. Graduate support remains largely reactive after completion. Building the infrastructure now allows King’s to translate more relationships into opportunity, protect valuable international relationships, widen purposeful global experience, strengthen graduate transition and scale before fragmented processes become a constraint on programme ambition.
caseForChange.intendedChange: King’s moves from fragmented relationship, opportunity, funding and graduate-transition activity towards connected employability and experiential infrastructure. Domestic external relationships are converted into student-ready opportunities through dedicated translation and operational capacity; staff and partners work through clearer routes and common processes; a broader range of students can access purposeful global experience; students have more consistent access to meaningful experience and financial support; employer engagement is stronger in the UK and priority international markets; graduates at greater risk of poorer outcomes can be identified and supported proactively; and King’s can evidence both Education and Student Success benefits and wider recruitment and reputation benefits from the same institutional capability.

problemSolved: King’s does not yet consistently convert its distributed external relationships, employability capability, global partnerships, alumni connection and opportunity funding into a coherent supply of accessible domestic and international experience and sustained support through the transition into graduate destinations.
whatChanges: King’s establishes connected domestic opportunity-translation, experiential, international employer-engagement, global mobility, access and graduate-transition infrastructure that can generate and sustain more opportunities, reduce operational friction, widen purposeful international experience, remove financial barriers and intervene proactively where graduates need additional support.
